questions.question_text: Two perpendicular arms enclose a right angle. A ray between them splits it into $32^{\circ}$ and $x^{\circ}$. Find $x$.

options.why: Subtracts $32^{\circ}$ from the straight-line total of $180^{\circ}$ instead of the right-angle total.
Subtracts $32^{\circ}$ from a full turn of $360^{\circ}$ instead of a right angle.
Assumes the two adjacent angles are equal without an equal-angle given.

questions.solution_text:
$x+32=90$ (angles in a right angle).
$x=90-32=58$.
The missing angle is $58^{\circ}$.

questions.question_text: Two adjacent angles on a straight line are $118^{\circ}$ and $x^{\circ}$. Find $x$.

options.why: Finds the difference between $118^{\circ}$ and $90^{\circ}$ instead of subtracting from the straight-line total.
Subtracts $118^{\circ}$ from $270^{\circ}$, counting three right angles instead of a half-turn.
Subtracts $118^{\circ}$ from the full-turn total of $360^{\circ}$ instead of the straight-line total.

questions.solution_text:
$x+118=180$ (angles on a straight line).
$x=180-118=62$.
The missing angle is $62^{\circ}$.

questions.question_text: Four angles fill a complete turn around a point. Three are $44^{\circ}$, $57^{\circ}$ and $69^{\circ}$. Find the fourth angle.

options.why: Subtracts the known total of $170^{\circ}$ from a half-turn of $180^{\circ}$ instead of a full turn.
Finds the difference between the known total of $170^{\circ}$ and a right angle of $90^{\circ}$.
Adds the three known angles but does not subtract their sum from the full-turn total. Two straight angles total $360^{\circ}$, not $180^{\circ}$.

questions.solution_text:
$x+44+57+69=360$ (angles at a point).
$x+170=360$.
$x=190$.
The fourth angle is $190^{\circ}$.
